info.title: Luna Shopper API
info.description: Public API for the Luna Shopper shared shopping lists. Response schemas are projected from the same JSON Schemas the services validate their broker messages against, so what is documented here is what the wire carries.

username.description: Your display name in this zone. Omit it to be called by your global username.
Your display name in this zone. Omit it to be called by your global username.
Your display name in this zone. Omit it to be called by your global username.

permissions.description: The complete permission set for this membership. Empty revokes access.

itemIds.description: The catalog products this line stands for (plan 0048, section 1.1). Picking a group in the composer sends that group’s members here. Absent or empty is a free text line, which stays first class.
Replace the line’s product set (plan 0048, section 1.1); an empty array clears it back to free text. A whole set and not an add or a remove, for the same reason reorder takes the whole order.

delta.description: How many to add, or a negative number to take off. Never zero. The resulting quantity has to stay within the line quantity bounds.

sourceUserId.description: Account whose data is taken from

targetUserId.description: Account the data is moved into

propagation.description: How far the change travels. Omitted means GLOBAL_ONLY: the zones where you chose a different name keep it.

externalBrandKey.description: The chain's stable identity across discovery runs, the Wikidata QID (plan 0038, section 5.4). Owner editable: the QID splits `Carrefour` from `Carrefour Express`, which may or may not be wanted.
The chain's stable identity across discovery runs, the Wikidata QID (plan 0038, section 5.4). Owner editable: the QID splits `Carrefour` from `Carrefour Express`, which may or may not be wanted.

priceScopeId.description: The scope this store prices against (plan 0038, section 5.1). Omit it and the store gets a STORE scope of its own, which is exactly how catalog behaved before scopes existed.

externalRef.description: The discovery provider’s own reference, e.g. `node/1156230891`. Not a reliable primary identity: an OSM element changes id and type when a shop is remapped from a node to a building way.

priceScopeId.description: The scope this store prices against (plan 0038, section 5.1). Omit it and the store gets a STORE scope of its own, which is exactly how catalog behaved before scopes existed.

externalRef.description: The discovery provider’s own reference, e.g. `node/1156230891`. Not a reliable primary identity: an OSM element changes id and type when a shop is remapped from a node to a building way.

externalKey.description: The source's own key for the scope, e.g. Mercadona's warehouse. A string and never an integer: the key comes back as both a numeric code (`4661`) and a city slug (`mad3`).

slug.description: A stable handle for admin tooling and tests: lower case words separated by single dashes.

referenceUnit.description: The unit this group’s members are compared in.

ean.description: The barcode: the only identifier that joins a product across chains (plan 0038, section 2.5). Unique across the catalog when present.

unitSize.description: Without it `defaultUnit` says nothing: "LITER" is not a size.

productGroupId.description: The product group this belongs to (plan 0048, section 1): the statement that this milk is comparable with that milk. Owner curation, never assigned automatically.

ean.description: The barcode: the only identifier that joins a product across chains (plan 0038, section 2.5). Unique across the catalog when present.

unitSize.description: Without it `defaultUnit` says nothing: "LITER" is not a size.

productGroupId.description: Assign, reassign or (with null) unassign the product’s group (plan 0048, section 1).

priceScopeId.description: The price scope, not the store (plan 0038, section 5.2). A chain that publishes one price per warehouse stores one row per warehouse instead of twelve identical ones per city.

unitPrice.description: The source's own normalized price per reference unit, stored verbatim and never recomputed (plan 0038, section 2.4).

unitPriceLabel.description: The source's own label for `unitPrice`. Text and not a unit: a product labelled `100 ml` carries a per litre number, and `lv` means washing machine loads.

available.description: A per store override meaning "someone checked this specific shop". Null clears it and defers to the scope’s answer, which is not the same as saying "not available here".

priceScopeId.description: The scope a REFRESH writes its prices for. Required for REFRESH.

postalCode.description: Required for STORE_DISCOVERY. It decides the price scope through the chain’s own resolver; the radius below decides the store list. Two questions, two sources (plan 0038, section 2.8).

radiusMetres.description: A radius, never a postcode filter: two thirds of OSM stores carry no postcode, and a postal code’s bounding box spans a whole city. 3 km returned 26 supermarkets around 14013.

brandKeys.description: Restrict the report to these `brand:wikidata` keys.

supermarketId.description: Attach to an existing chain instead of resolving it by `brand:wikidata`.

category.description: Override the category the source’s own tree mapped to. Mercadona has 26 top level categories against our 12, so the mapping is lossy by construction.

enabled.description: A source is created disabled. Turning fetching on for a third party is a decision made explicitly, never a side effect of describing the chain.

config.description: Adapter specific settings. For `mercadona-api` this is where the resolved `warehouse` lives, e.g. `{ "warehouse": "4661" }`.

workers.description: How many requests may be in flight at once: sockets and memory. NOT the rate — see maxRequestsPerSecond.

maxRequestsPerSecond.description: The politeness rate, held by one token bucket every worker blocks on. Watch for 429s and treat any as a signal to halve this rather than to retry harder.

zoneId.description: The zone the list is in.

listId.description: The only list this turn may touch.

transcript.description: The conversation so far, oldest first.

scope.description: Narrow this turn to one list. Omit it for the ordinary assistant.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Whole seconds before another request of this kind is accepted.

auth.RetryAfterResult.description: The request was accepted. `retryAfterSeconds` is how long before another is accepted; a refusal returns the same field on the error envelope with what is actually left. Count down the number you were given rather than assuming a fixed wait.

ProblemDetails.description: The RFC 7807 error envelope, served as `application/problem+json`. `message` is already translated to the request locale, so a client can show it without knowing any backend error code; `code` is the stable value to branch on.

type.description: A URI identifying the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

code.description: The stable machine code the client branches on.

detail.description: Extra context about this occurrence, when there is any.

message.description: The message to show the user, in the request's locale.

correlationId.description: Identifies this request across every service log; quote it in a bug report.

errors.description: Per field validation messages. Present only when `code` is `validation_failed`.

retryAfterSeconds.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying. Present only when `code` is `rate_limited`. Read this rather than assuming a fixed wait: the limits are enforced per gateway pod, so two requests from the same client can legitimately return different numbers.

stats.PlatformStatsResponse.description: Platform totals. Either block is `null` when that service did not answer: a broken service degrades the figure rather than taking down the public page.

measuredAt.description: When the snapshot was taken, so the 60 second cache is visible rather than hidden.

An authenticated caller gets `data` alone.

tokens.description: Present only when the caller was anonymous.
